papers.title: Echoes of Trauma: The Role of Self-Esteem Between Adverse Childhood Experiences and Intimate Partner Violence Victimization.
papers.abstract: The association between adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and intimate partner violence victimization (IPVV) is well-documented. However, little is known about whether this association varies by self-esteem during emerging adulthood, a developmental period marked by increasing self-exploration and exposure to intimate relationships. This study examines whether self-esteem moderates the association between ACEs and IPVV in emerging adulthood. Data were drawn from South Korean emerging adults aged 18 to 29 with dating experience (N = 953). Negative binomial regression models were estimated, followed by average marginal effects and Johnson-Neyman style floodlight analysis. The results show that the association between physical ACEs and physical IPVV was significantly positive at lower levels of self-esteem. However, two disjoint crossover patterns were found between neglect and emotional IPVV (EIPVV). Neglect was negatively associated with EIPVV at a lower level of self-esteem but positively associated at a higher level. Findings highlight subtype-specific ACE-IPVV pathways and caution against treating self-esteem as a uniformly protective factor. The study contributes to trauma-informed IPVV prevention by emphasizing the need to consider both childhood adversity histories and the quality of self-esteem during emerging adulthood.

papers.title: Freedom With Fear: Post-Release Psychological Trauma Among Survivors of Enforced Disappearance in Bangladesh.
papers.journal: International journal of mental health nursing
papers.abstract: Enforced disappearance is designed to erase a person; those who return alive carry that erasure into everyday life. This qualitative study examined post-release trauma among survivors of enforced disappearance in Bangladesh. Working within a constructivist paradigm, we conducted 36 semi-structured in-depth interviews between January and March 2025 with survivors recruited through established human rights organizations, and analysed the data with NVivo using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis. Three themes were developed. First, persistent hypervigilance: ordinary objects, sounds, colours and bodily sensations present during captivity, among them a brand of soap, a white van, dripping water and cold air, reactivated fear, panic and collapse, with triggers indexed to the sensory conditions of each person's detention rather than shared across the sample. Second, the persistent shadow of humiliation: forced nudity, sexual mockery and dehumanizing treatment continued to shape dignity, self-worth and intimate relationships long after release. Third, emotional numbness: protective silence towards family, fractured bonds and compounded grief left reintegration incomplete. Read together, the themes describe not discrete after-effects but three registers of one continuing condition, sustained by an environment in which those responsible remain unaccountable. Mental health nurses working with this population should map the individual's sensory environment with consent, address humiliation-related shame explicitly and treat safety as an ongoing achievement rather than a settled fact.

papers.title: Associations between empathy dimensions, love language expression, and relationship satisfaction among university students in Northern Cyprus.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to explore relationships among aspects of empathy, love language expression, and relationship satisfaction among university students. We also examined attachment styles as a theoretical framework; however, severe measurement limitations prevented valid inferences about attachment patterns. METHOD: We used a cross-sectional study of 513 students in Northern Cyprus (M = 20.99 years; 56.3% female) using the Relationship Scales Questionnaire (RSQ), Five Love Languages Scale (FLLS), Basic Empathy Scale (BES), and Relationship Assessment Scale (RAS). We used snowball sampling with power analysis showing adequate power to detect medium effects. However, we found important limitations in the measurement: the RSQ showed unacceptably low reliability (α = 0.27 to 0.61), and attachment measures are therefore uninterpretable. RESULTS: After revising initial errors in scoring, we found that expression of love language frequency was positively correlated with relationship satisfaction (r = .45), with Quality Time (r = .48) and Gift-Giving (r = .45) being the strongest associations. Cognitive empathy (r = .39) was significantly more highly related to satisfaction than affective empathy (r = .15). Due to the extremely low reliability of the RSQ (0.27-0.61; α), we cannot make any inferences regarding attachment patterns. Gender differences had a small to medium effect, with females displaying greater empathy and increased use of some love languages. CONCLUSION: The expression of love language and cognitive empathy are positively related to relationship satisfaction in this sample of university students. However, severe measurement restrictions using the attachment scale preclude any conclusions about attachment patterns. Upcoming research should use psychometrically sound measures, such as the Experiences in Close Relationships-Revised (ECR-R) scale.

papers.title: Anatomical anomalies of the arteries of the head and neck - are they always the cause of fatal haemorrhages following tonsillectomy?
papers.abstract: We present a case of fatal delayed post-operative haemorrhage following palatine tonsillectomy in a 21-year-old man. Massive haemorrhage occurred 58 hours after surgery. Despite emergency airway management and haemorrhage control, the patient died from hypovolaemic shock. Post-mortem examination revealed transection of the right facial artery approximately 1 cm from its origin from the external carotid artery. The precise mechanism of the arterial injury could not be established because neither preoperative nor post-mortem vascular imaging was available. An unusually close relationship between the facial artery and the tonsillar fossa may have predisposed to vascular injury, while delayed vascular complications, including pseudoaneurysm formation, represent alternative possible mechanisms. Fatal post-tonsillectomy haemorrhage is rare but may result from major arterial injury. Autopsy examination remains important in establishing the source of fatal bleeding, while vascular imaging, including PMCTA, may provide additional information concerning the mechanism of injury.

papers.title: Dyadic Effects of Personality on Sexual Behavior and Experiences in Older Adulthood.
papers.abstract: Sex is a central component of intimate relationships. However, much of our knowledge of the psychological factors shaping satisfying sexual lives is limited to younger adults. We examined individual (i.e., actor) and partner effects of the Big Five personality traits on sexual outcomes (i.e., sexual frequency, sexual and relational quality, and sexual dysfunction) among 953 older opposite-sex couples followed over five years as part of the National Social Life, Health, and Aging Project (Mage = 70.60 years, SD = 7.92). Individual and partner conscientiousness were linked to more frequent sex and greater physical and emotional relationship quality, whereas neuroticism was linked to more sexual problems and lower satisfaction. Individual and partner agreeableness were associated with more satisfying sex and relationships. Individual extraversion was positively associated with higher sexual and relational satisfaction and fewer problems, but partner extraversion effects were largely non-significant. Both actor and partner openness were related to poorer evaluations of sex and relationships, but had limited associations with sexual problems. Some gender differences emerged, with more nuanced partner effects for women. Longitudinal analyses indicated that most associations wavered in strength over time. These findings highlight the role of both partners' personality traits in encouraging sexual and relational well-being in older adulthood.

papers.title: Bomb-radiocarbon validated otoliths reveal 130-year lifespans and declining recruitment for blue sucker Cycleptus elongatus of the Upper Missouri River, Montana, USA.
papers.abstract: Validated age-based life history traits are crucial towards understanding the biological complexity of the natural world. The blue sucker Cycleptus elongatus is a migratory freshwater fish of the family Catostomidae native to North America. For decades, there has been conservation concern for the species across much of its range, including populations with skewed size distributions indicative of recruitment bottlenecks. Nonetheless, no validated age-based life history information exists for the species, which is a major knowledge gap. Using thin-sectioned otoliths validated by bomb radiocarbon dating we found that individual blue sucker often live more than 100 years, exhibit sexually-size dimorphic growth, increased fecundity with size, and spot-pigmentation with age. Across 42 individuals from the Upper Missouri River, Montana, we observed a maximum lifespan of 131 years, which is 70 years older than previously reported. Furthermore, 64-76% of individuals were from hatch years that pre-date the completion of Fort Peck Dam (1940), Canyon Ferry Dam (1954), and Tiber Dam (1956), which suggests recruitment failure is more likely in the post-dam era. Our findings redefine our understanding of blue sucker, parallel recent population demographic discoveries for buffalofishes (Ictiobus spp.), and further identify the diversity of the centenarian catostomid guild.

papers.title: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China.
papers.abstract: Homo erectus represents one of the longest-persisting hominin species, with a geographic range from Africa to eastern Eurasia from approximately 1.9 million years ago1 to 108 thousand years ago (ka)2. Despite this, there are still large gaps in our understanding of the adaptation capabilities of this species and the extent of its persistence in China. Assumptions over ecological preferences based on the Trinil3, Sangiran4 and Ngandong2 (in Java) open woodland-grassland mosaics have persisted, combined with limited direct stable carbon isotope measurements in Asia. Here we present a rich temporal and environmental context for nine hominin teeth, eight of which were morphologically and genetically identified as H. erectus5, found in two sister caves in Guangxi province, southern China. We modelled 43 radiometric ages from five dating techniques to establish a timeline for H. erectus presence in this region. Stable and clumped isotopes and trace elements from teeth were used to establish the dominant environments and their behavioural responses. We show that H. erectus was present in southern China between 324 and 184 ka, which is substantially more recent than previously established in this region for unequivocally H. erectus fossils at approximately 400 ka. The evidence suggests that they were persisting in closed rainforest ecosystems, thought to be the domain of only Homo sapiens, and were demonstrating long-term mobility and ecological flexibility. This evidence challenges the assumptions over the ecological preferences and behavioural limitations of H. erectus.

papers.title: The Tapetum: Historical Evolution, Anatomical Insights, and Contemporary Neurosurgical Relevance.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The tapetum is a thin commissural fiber layer originating predominantly from the splenium of the corpus callosum and forming part of the lateral wall of the atrium and temporal horn of the lateral ventricle. Although surgically relevant, its historical development has received limited attention. This review examines the evolution of the anatomical concept of the tapetum from early descriptions of interhemispheric and ventricular anatomy to contemporary fiber-dissection and tractographic perspectives. METHODS: A narrative historical review was conducted using classical neuroanatomical texts from the sixteenth to twentieth centuries and contemporary studies identified through PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. Historical primary sources and modern anatomical, surgical, and imaging studies were reviewed. RESULTS: Early concepts of interhemispheric connectivity arose from descriptions of the corpus callosum and ventricular anatomy. Johann Christian Reil formally defined the tapetum in 1809 as a carpet-like layer of callosal fibers lining the lateral ventricular wall. Nineteenth-century anatomists, including Burdach, Arnold, Gratiolet, Flechsig, Meynert, and the Dejerines, refined its topography while highlighting uncertainties regarding adjacent projection and association pathways. Twentieth-century fiber dissection, particularly the Klingler method, enabled three-dimensional visualization, while modern diffusion imaging and tractography supported the interpretation of the tapetum as a thin laminar extension of splenial callosal fibers. CONCLUSION: The tapetum concept evolved from descriptive ventricular anatomy to a fiber-based understanding of posterior interhemispheric connectivity. Its close relationship with the optic radiation and lateral ventricular wall underscores its relevance in contemporary approaches to the atrium and temporal horn.

papers.title: Lichen Sclerosus and the Genital Anatomy: Impact on Sexual Function.
papers.abstract: Lichen sclerosus (LS), a chronic inflammatory dermatosis that primarily affects the anogenital region, leads to progressive architectural distortion with significant sexual sequelae. In women, chronic inflammation and scarring result in flattening and resorption of the labia minora, clitoral hood fusion and burial, introital stenosis, and vulvar atrophy. Advanced disease may cause fissures, erosions, and fourchette fusion, contributing to dyspareunia, apareunia, and even difficulty in achieving orgasm. Nearly 60% of women with vulvar LS report sexual dysfunction, with pain during intercourse being the most common complaint. Anatomic narrowing reduced clitoral sensation, and fear of pain further impair both arousal and lubrication, compounding dysfunction and negatively affecting intimate relationships and body image. In men, genital LS most often involves the glans and foreskin, leading to hypopigmented plaques, progressive sclerosis, phimosis, painful erections, and, when severe, urethral strictures. Penile soreness from active inflammation and structural restriction contribute to dyspareunia and reduced sexual satisfaction. Psychologic factors, including embarrassment and anxiety, further exacerbate sexual impairment. Greater disease severity correlates with a worse sexual quality of life. Despite its profound impact, sexual dysfunction in LS remains both under-recognized and under-discussed in clinical practice. Early recognition and disease-suppressing therapy are essential to prevent irreversible anatomic changes. Comprehensive management should include the proactive assessment of sexual function, addressing both structural and psychosocial contributors to optimize patient well-being.

papers.title: Dermatology Disease Associations with Masturbation: Myth vs Facts.
papers.abstract: The act of masturbation is defined as stimulating one's own genitalia for sexual pleasure. Despite its associated stigmatization, masturbation has persisted throughout the entirety of human history, with origins dating back to over 40 million years ago. Myths surrounding masturbation and its effects have evolved and continue to spread. Some are tangentially based on facts while others are simply myths. Dermatologic associations with masturbation have been featured heavily in these myths, including the beliefs that acne or hair changes can be induced by this behavior. However, there are also many fact-based associations between masturbation and skin issues; infections, allergic reactions, "sex-flush", and Mondor's disease are among the most well-understood. Addressing and describing the distinction between myth and fact is important, both to educate healthcare providers about potential patient concerns and to dispel confusion. Herein we provide clarification on these issues and open the discussion on a topic that deserves the level of consideration corresponding to its prevalence.

papers.title: Effects of connective tissue diseases on self-image and sexual confidence.
papers.abstract: Connective tissue diseases (CTDs) are chronic, multisystem autoimmune disorders associated with substantial physical and psychosocial morbidity. Visible cutaneous manifestations, pain, fatigue, functional limitations, psychiatric comorbidity, and treatment-related changes in appearance may profoundly affect self-image, body image, intimate relationships, and sexual well-being. This narrative review examines the effects of CTDs commonly encountered in dermatologic practice on self-image and sexual confidence. Across lupus erythematosus, scleroderma spectrum disorders, Sjögren syndrome, dermatomyositis, rheumatoid arthritis, and Behçet disease, sexual dysfunction is highly prevalent and reflects the complex interplay of cutaneous and systemic disease manifestations, psychologic distress, and altered self-perception. Despite substantial effects on quality of life, sexual health concerns remain infrequently addressed in routine clinical practice. Greater clinician awareness, proactive screening, and multidisciplinary approaches integrating dermatologic and psychologic care may help address these unmet needs and promote more comprehensive, patient-centered care.

papers.title: Substance use and recovery in the perinatal period: A cracked window of opportunity?
papers.journal: The International journal on drug policy
papers.abstract: Pregnancy and early parenthood are increasingly framed as a 'window of opportunity' for engaging women with substance use (SU) problems in treatment and recovery. Yet, when support becomes organized around the perinatal period and child, important questions arise regarding how recovery is understood and sustained. This qualitative study explored which factors shape women's trajectories of SU and recovery, and the role of the perinatal period and child within these processes. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 12 mothers in Flanders (Belgium) who initiated recovery during pregnancy or early parenthood, and analyzed using inductive thematic analysis. Findings indicate that women's trajectories were embedded in longstanding experiences of childhood adversity, mental health problems, and relational vulnerability. Both intimate relationships and SU frequently functioned as ways of coping with distress and unmet relational needs. Against this background, the child emerges as an ambivalent subject at the personal level, in intimate relationships, in family relations, and in recovery and care trajectories. While the child often provided meaning, hope, and motivation for change, women also projected expectations of connection, security, stability, and recovery onto the child. The findings suggest that emotional and relational needs previously sought through intimate relationships and SU were often reorganized around the child. Care practices may unintentionally reinforce this when treatment engagement becomes closely linked to child welfare and the prevention of child removal. The perinatal period may therefore be better understood as a 'cracked window of opportunity': while it can facilitate treatment engagement, overemphasizing the child as the primary catalyst for change, without simultaneously addressing underlying relational and trauma-related vulnerabilities, may contribute to the intergenerational transmission of relational vulnerability. papers.title: Genomic characterization, synteny, and cold-responsive expression of Soybean HD-ZIP IV transcription factor candidates.
papers.abstract: Homeodomain-leucine zipper (HD-ZIP) transcription factors regulate plant development and responses to environmental stress. This study characterized selected soybean (Glycine max) HD-ZIP IV candidates by integrating domain screening, genomic mapping, phylogenetic comparison, evolutionary analysis, general co-expression networks, and secondary analysis of cold-stress expression data. A broader domain audit recovered 95 loci with family-associated architectures, comprising 54 with I/II patterns, 12 with III patterns, and 29 with IV patterns. Comparison with a published 88-gene inventory established correspondences for 86 entries, of which 82 satisfied the joint-domain criteria; recovery therefore remained conditional rather than demonstrating completeness. The 29 selected IV-pattern candidates were distributed across 15 chromosomes and encoded representative proteins of 713-836 amino acids. Domain architecture and placement alongside Arabidopsis IV reference proteins supported their classification. Of 160 candidate pairs, 122 yielded finite NG86 estimates, all with Ka/Ks ratios below 1.0, consistent with purifying constraint. However, 79 finite pairs had Ks > 2, limiting duplication dating. The general co-expression network contained 617 nodes and 802 edges; candidate rankings differed between connectivity and betweenness metrics. Cold-stress expression statistics were estimable for 22 candidates. At adjusted P < 0.01 and |log2 fold change| ≥ 1, genotype-dependent temporal contrasts identified 11, 8, and 8 candidates at 2, 4, and 8 h, respectively. Gm.HDZ6, Gm.HDZ19, and Gm.HDZ22 met these criteria at all three times. These findings identify candidates for functional investigation while distinguishing evolutionary constraints and expression associations from complete family recovery, reliable duplication chronology, and causal mechanisms of cold tolerance.

papers.title: Hydrogen-Bond-Induced Dual Structural Response in Amide-Functionalized Self-Assembled Monolayers.
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry letters
papers.abstract: Internal functionalization can reorganize intermolecular interactions across a self-assembled monolayer (SAM), yet its depth-dependent consequences remain poorly understood. Here, molecular dynamics simulations and vibrational sum-frequency generation (VSFG) spectroscopy reveal a dual structural response in N-(2-mercaptoethyl)heptanamide SAMs on Au(111). A persistent intermolecular hydrogen-bonding network suppresses conformational fluctuations between the Au-S interface and the amide plane. Above this plane, however, the larger volume of the amide increases alkyl-chain separation, weakens van der Waals coupling, and enhances conformational flexibility with temperature. Thus, a hydrogen-bond-stabilized, solid-like lower region coexists with a weakly coupled, liquid-like upper region. Simulated VSFG spectra reproduce the observed terminal CH3 stretching-mode intensities, including the enhanced asymmetric response. This response occurs without a correspondingly large average methyl tilt angle because inequivalent molecular environments produce broad, heterogeneous orientation distributions. Consequently, the conventional assignment of a single methyl tilt angle from VSFG intensity ratio breaks down for internally functionalized SAMs.

papers.title: Site-Dependent Structural Effects of R1 Spin Labeling in an Aβ42 Protofilament Characterized by Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
papers.abstract: Site-directed spin labeling coupled with electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) is used to characterize structural features in amyloid fibrils, but whether the nitroxide spin label R1 perturbs the structure it reports remains unclear. Molecular dynamics simulations compared wild-type Aβ42 with ten R1-labeled variants in a five-layer protofilament derived from the type I human-brain fibril structure. We quantified nitroxide proximity, regional interlayer packing, backbone hydrogen bonding, R1-protein contacts, and R1 side-chain rotamer sampling. Simulated nitroxide contacts reproduced the experimental distinction between sites with strong and weak spin-spin interactions, although some sites deviated from the trend. Regional interlayer organization and backbone hydrogen bonding were preserved relative to wild-type. However, structural responses were site-dependent and sometimes extended beyond the labeling site. The 32R1 system produced the largest rearrangement of the C-terminal tail. Comparison with the corresponding unlabeled cysteine control showed smaller perturbation, indicating that the response at position 32 arose primarily from the R1 label rather than the cysteine substitution itself. Thus, R1 generally preserved the protofilament architecture and reflected the local packing environment while producing label-specific structural adjustments. These results support R1 as a reporter of local packing in Aβ42 fibrils and demonstrate the value of site-resolved comparisons for identifying label-induced effects.

papers.title: Dual-responsive poly(N-isopropylacrylamide-co-methacrylic acid) hydrogels: role and synergies of pH and temperature in tailoring hydrogel responsiveness.
papers.abstract: Stimuli-responsive hydrogels based on poly(N-isopropylacrylamide-co-methacrylic acid) (P(NIPAM m -co-MAA n )) have well-established dual pH- and thermoresponsive behaviour. Here, we investigate how a relatively low MAA content (10, 20, or 30 mol%) impacts on the physicochemical properties and coupled thermo- and pH-responsive behaviour, bringing pH dominance over temperature. Crosslinked P(NIPAM m -co-MAA n ) hydrogels were synthesised by photopolymerization from varying proportions of the thermoresponsive monomer NIPAM and the pH-responsive monomer MAA (10, 20, or 30 mol% MAA), using 1 mol% N,N'-methylenebisacrylamide (BIS) as crosslinker. Swelling, compressive elastic modulus, water contact angle, pore size, transition temperature, and enthalpy of phase transition were studied as a function of temperature and pH for the P(NIPAM m -co-MAA n ) hydrogels. The pH-dependent behaviour of the thermoresponsive copolymer hydrogels is attributed to hydrogen bonding interactions between NIPAM and MAA units, predominant at low pH, and to the enhanced hydration of ionised MAA carboxylate groups at high pH. Although the MAA content did not exceed 30 mol%, it played a key role in determining hydrogel properties. Notably, pH had a stronger effect than temperature on hydrogel responsiveness, and at high pH, hydrogels largely lose their ability to undergo volume collapse above the volume phase transition temperature (VPTT).

papers.title: Mg(II)/H-Bonding Catalyst Design for Asymmetric Amination-Protonation Reaction.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Given the strong interaction between amine and ketone groups, which often act as catalyst-substrate partners via iminium ion catalysis, the catalytic asymmetric aza-conjugate addition of common cyclic amines to unsaturated enones has never been successfully achieved. This model reaction is inherently challenging due to both the self-racemization of the amino-ketone products and the autocatalysis arising from the amine-ketone interaction. Consequently, this most straightforward and efficient route to chiral γ-amino alcohols remains unrealized to date. Herein, through the rational design of a novel Mg(II)/H-bonding catalytic strategy based on newly developed trihydroxyl chiral ligands, we have successfully suppressed the self-activation pathway between amines and conjugated enones, thereby achieving the desired amination-protonation reaction with high enantioselectivities. This new catalytic system proves highly effective for the one-pot synthesis of diverse chiral γ-amino alcohols bearing tertiary or quaternary stereocenters. Mechanistic investigations, including the identification of the formed metal complex and the true catalytically active species, the study of key transition states, and the elucidation of the coordination details of the Mg(II)/H-bonding catalyst through DFT-optimized processes, support a plausible mechanism for the asymmetric amination-protonation process.

papers.title: Beyond Swelling: Electrochemical Doping Tunes the Balance between Ion Compensation and Exchange in a Hydrated Organic Mixed Ionic-Electronic Conductor.
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.abstract: Organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs) couple electronic doping to ion compensation and water reorganization. As doping increasing, molecular reorganization within the polymer-ion-water environment is thought to underlie the often nonmonotonic response of OMIEC devices, yet this process is essential for the understanding of structure-function relationship in related OMIEC devices but remains unclear. Although advanced operando measurements can resolve charge-state-dependent counterion localization within ordered OMIEC domains, jointly tracking electronic charging, explicit ion compensation, hydration, and molecular exchange across doping remains challenging; conventional simulations likewise do not allow these coupled variables to evolve together under constant electrochemical potential. To address these limitations under experimentally relevant electrochemical conditions, we develop an ion-regulated quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) grand-canonical molecular dynamics framework that operates at constant electrochemical potential and samples OMIECs across experimentally relevant doping levels. Experimental 23Na and 35Cl nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectra and layer-resolved computational sum-frequency-generation (SFG) spectra validate the polymer microstructure and polymer-electrolyte interfacial model. The simulations reveal a doping-dependent reorganization mechanism and identify a distinct compensation-exchange balance at the charging level associated with the experimental carrier-mobility maximum. With increasing doping, water-side-chain hydrogen bonding weakens and the glycol-rich environment crosses over from Na+ organization to Cl--dominated compensation. Near the mobility maximum, persistent Na+ environments and a long-lived Na+-Cl- motif coexist with a more rapidly exchanging Cl- population. Further charging disrupts this balance, producing either kinetically trapped Cl- or a more highly hydrated, rapidly exchanging environment.

papers.title: Subzero self-assembly of a glucose-based surfactant in ethylene glycol-water mixture.
papers.journal: Journal of colloid and interface science
papers.abstract: Subzero surfactant self-assembly in alcohol-water media provides a route to cryogenic soft materials, but the thermodynamic and kinetic origins of temperature-driven aggregate reorganization remain insufficiently understood. Here, we investigate the temperature-regulated self-assembly of the glucose-based surfactant, (Z)-N-ethyl-N-(2,3,4,5,6-pentahydroxyhexyl) docos-13-enamide (UC22GEt), in ethylene glycol (EG)-water (50/50, v/v). UC22GEt combines a polyhydroxyl glucamide headgroup, a tertiary amide linkage, and an unsaturated C22 chain, enabling coupled responses of solvent hydrogen bonding, amide association, and hydrophobic-chain packing to temperature. Optical transmittance and differential scanning calorimetry reveal a subzero upper critical solution temperature transition. Nile Red fluorescence reveals a nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the critical micelle concentration (CMC), while model-based thermodynamic analysis suggests a temperature-dependent balance between enthalpic and entropic contributions. Small-angle X-ray scattering and cryogenic transmission electron microscopy demonstrate a temperature-induced morphological evolution from onion-like multilamellar vesicles (OMLVs) to a vesicle/ spherical micelle coexistence state and finally to spherical micelles. Time-resolved fluorescence further identifies a two-stage transformation governed by kinetic constraints. Upon heating, Raman spectra reveal changes in hydrogen-bonding and alkyl-chain environments, while rheology shows a transition from weak-gel-like to nearly Newtonian behavior. By linking molecular interactions, mesoscale morphology, thermodynamic driving forces, transformation kinetics, and macroscopic rheology within a single system, this work advances subzero surfactant studies beyond phenomenological phase observation. These results establish an integrated framework for subzero curvature regulation and provide design principles for cryogenic and temperature-responsive soft materials.

papers.title: High-entropy carbides: structure, synthesis and catalytic applications.
papers.abstract: High-entropy carbides (HECs) - multicomponent interstitial compounds with multiple transition metals distributed on a shared metal sublattice and carbon occupying interstitial sites - expand the catalytic design space beyond conventional unary and binary carbides, owing to their diverse local coordination environments, tunable metal-carbon bonding, and rich defect chemistry. Nevertheless, HECs, especially nanoscale HECs, remain far less developed than high-entropy alloys and conventional transition-metal carbides. Their vast compositional space is paired with tightly coupled challenges in phase formation, carbon stoichiometry, elemental mixing uniformity, surface chemistry and structure, all of which are difficult to regulate independently. This Review establishes a structure-synthesis-catalysis framework for the field. We examine the crystal chemistry, thermodynamic descriptors, and computational design strategies for navigating the extensive HEC composition space, and compare conventional thermal processing with emerging ultrafast synthetic routes. We further define the core structural evidence required to rigorously verify phase purity, intraparticle elemental distributions, carbon vacancies, and reaction-induced surface reconstruction. We then critically assess reported catalytic applications, distinguish well-substantiated findings from prospective opportunities, and identify key priorities for scalable synthesis, operando characterization, and predictive catalyst design. By bridging materials design principles with working-state structural verification, this Review provides a rigorous foundation for the rational development of HECs as functional catalytic materials.

papers.title: The dual-directional chemical bridge: decoupling the interfacial roles of spacer cations in two-dimensional/three-dimensional (2D/3D) perovskites.
papers.abstract: 2D/3D perovskite heterointerfaces are widely used to improve the operational stability of perovskite solar cells, but their molecular role is often described mainly in terms of surface passivation. Bulky spacer cations coordinate under-coordinated surface sites, form hydrogen-bonding networks, and suppress ion migration. Simultaneously, poorly coupled organic tails may increase tunnelling distance and weaken charge extraction. This review discusses bulky cations as dual-directional chemical bridges rather than simple insulating barriers. The polar headgroup anchors the inorganic lattice through coordination, hydrogen bonding, and conformational restriction, whereas the exposed organic segment may tune interfacial energetics through dipolar effects, orbital overlap, and intermolecular π-π coupling. We compare the chemical mechanisms governing downward lattice stabilization and upward electronic communication, and highlight surface-sensitive tools required to probe molecular orientation, local potential shifts, and buried interfacial interactions. Together, these considerations support a design framework in which spacer-cation arrays are treated as organized interfacial ensembles. In such ensembles, geometric matching and multiple non-covalent interactions may help connect lattice stabilization with charge extraction, providing a chemical basis for mitigating the efficiency-stability trade-off.

papers.title: Exploring family support and conflict in intergenerational co-parenting families: scale development study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Existing family support scales often fail to capture the culturally specific structure and role expectations within Chinese families. This study aimed to develop and validate a culturally grounded, role-differentiated measure of family support and conflict among Chinese postpartum women in intergenerational co-parenting families. METHODS: Drawing on literature review, interviews, and principal component analysis, the Postpartum Family Interaction Scale (PFIS), comprising 12 factors across both support and conflict dimensions and distinguishing between partner and parental sources as perceived by postpartum women, was developed. A total of 528 postpartum women completed the scale. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), measurement invariance tests, internal consistency, construct validity, and predictive validity for postpartum depressive symptoms were examined. RESULTS: The PFIS presented a 12-factor structure with high reliability and validity. The 12 factors are intergenerational emotional/instrumental/ informational support, intergenerational emotional/instrumental/ informational conflict, partner emotional/instrumental/ informational support, and partner emotional/instrumental/ informational conflict. Specifically, partner emotional and informational support significantly predicted lower postpartum depressive symptoms, while partner emotional conflict and Intergenerational instrumental and informational conflict were positively associated with increased depression. CONCLUSIONS: The PFIS shows strong psychometric properties and provides a culturally and relationally nuanced tool for assessing postpartum family dynamics in Chinese families. It enables targeted assessment and supports the development of more precise, role-specific family interventions in maternal mental health support.

papers.title: The ARL4D-Interacting Protein GPR110 Promotes Neural Stem Cell Proliferation and Neuronal Differentiation in Radiation-Induced Brain Injury by Modulating Phosphorylation of the PI3K/Akt Pathway.
papers.abstract: High-dose whole-brain radiotherapy commonly causes cognitive dysfunction by impairing endogenous neurogenesis through oxidative stress, neuroinflammation and depletion of neural stem cells (NSCs). ADP-ribosylation factor-like protein 4D (ARL4D) is a small GTPase involved in cytoskeletal remodelling and cell-cycle regulation, whereas the adhesion G-protein-coupled receptor GPR110 (ADGRF1) is a known regulator of neurogenesis, neurite outgrowth and synaptic formation through cAMP signalling. Whether ARL4D and GPR110 interact to support NSC proliferation and neuronal differentiation after radiation injury remains unclear. Mouse NSCs (mNSCs) were engineered to overexpress ARL4D or GPR110, or to knock down GPR110, and were then exposed to 4 Gy X-rays where indicated. Cell viability and proliferation were evaluated using CCK-8 and EdU assays. Reciprocal co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) was performed to test the ARL4D-GPR110 interaction. Neuronal lineage commitment was assessed using the early neuronal marker DCX, the mature neuronal marker NeuN and the astrocytic marker GFAP, including quantification of the NeuN/GFAP ratio. Western blotting was used to evaluate PI3K/AKT pathway activity under basal and irradiation conditions, and LY294002 was used to test the functional requirement for PI3K/AKT signalling. Transcriptomic data and STRING protein-interaction analysis were used to identify ARL4D-associated networks. Transcriptomic profiling and STRING analysis identified Adgrf1 (GPR110) as a strongly up-regulated transcript and a predicted ARL4D-associated protein. Reciprocal Co-IP confirmed a physical interaction between endogenous ARL4D and GPR110 in mNSCs. After X-ray irradiation, ARL4D overexpression improved CCK-8 viability and EdU-positive proliferation, whereas GPR110 knockdown abolished this rescue. ARL4D or GPR110 overexpression increased DCX-positive and NeuN-positive cells and raised the NeuN/GFAP ratio. In irradiated cultures, ARL4D overexpression increased PI3K/AK

papers.title: From Medically Rooted Accounts of Perinatal Loss to Parents' Inner Worlds: Reorientation Toward Therapeutic Goals in Couples Therapy Consultations.
papers.abstract: This study examines the interactional work through which therapists and clients move from accounts of perinatal loss and trauma toward the formulation of therapeutic goals. We focus on how therapists engage with spouses' loss- and trauma-oriented talk and orient the interaction toward psychotherapeutically relevant goals. Using conversation analysis, we analyzed video recordings of eight couples' therapy processes comprising a total of 16 sessions conducted following perinatal loss. The findings enable us to delineate successive stages of therapeutic talk that mark the transition from the initial presentation of the problem to the formulation of therapeutic goals. These stages are (1) A Past-Oriented Shift in Problem Formulation, comprising (1.1) Naming the Loss as the Presenting Problem, (1.2) Describing the Circumstances of the Loss, and (1.3) Describing Emotional Pain Arising from the Loss, followed by (2) Formulation of Therapeutic Goals: Emotional Processing of Loss. The analysis shows that therapists initially adopt a receptive stance by using simple gist formulations. Over the course of the interaction, therapists move toward more complex upshot formulations, eventually framing the emotional processing of loss as a central therapeutic goal. Therapeutic talk following perinatal loss progresses gradually, acknowledging the trauma and ambiguity associated with this form of loss. Therapists facilitate this transition by moving from a receptive stance toward guiding patients into the emotional dimensions of their loss and its subsequent emotional processing.

papers.title: Sexual Satisfaction in Two-Spirit, Transgender, and Non-Binary Survivors of Childhood Sexual Abuse.
papers.abstract: Existing research on the impact of childhood sexual abuse (CSA) on adult sexual satisfaction has focused on the experiences of cisgender, heterosexual survivors. However, despite a high rate of victimization within the community, the long-term impacts on sexual wellbeing for two-spirit, transgender, and non-binary survivors (2STNB) have been neglected. The objectives of this study were to determine the impact of CSA on sexual satisfaction in a sample of 2STNB adults as well as factors that may influence this relationship. A community sample of 317 individuals was recruited through social media posts to complete an online survey, including measures of adverse childhood experiences, severity of CSA, sexual satisfaction, symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), experiences of intimate partner violence (IPV), and demographic questions. Results indicated that sexual satisfaction scores were not significantly related to CSA history and did not differ based on survivors' gender identities. Significant relationships were observed between the severity of abuse and PTSD scores, and the severity of abuse and IPV scores. Clinicians are nevertheless advised to carefully assess for CSA and to assess sexual satisfaction with 2STNB individuals and couples. Further research on the long-term effects of these experiences on the sexuality of 2STNB survivors would be valuable.

papers.title: Ayurveda Aphrodisiacs resulting in natural conception: A case report of erectile dysfunction induced primary infertility.
papers.journal: Journal of Ayurveda and integrative medicine
papers.abstract: Sexual dysfunction and infertility hold a close inter-relation affecting the marital, sexual and fertility status of an individual as well as the couple. The case presents a condition of male erectile dysfunction resulting in the infertile state of the couple. The case was treated with an integrative approach where the male was treated with Ayurveda Aphrodisiac (Vrushya chikitsa) preparations and the couple were subjected to multiple sessions of sexual counselling. The approach resulted in restoring the sexual function and gratification, in-turn making him capable of impregnating his partner. The female partner was equally satisfied with her sexual and fertility profile and delivered a healthy male child at term. A thorough evaluation and diagnosis is the cornerstone of any medical condition, and appropriate approach may aid in restoring the sexual and reproductive health through integrated approach.

papers.title: Examining the relationship between domestic violence awareness, self-compassion, and self-esteem in adult women.
papers.abstract: BackgroundDomestic violence is a serious social problem with physical, emotional, and psychological consequences. Self-esteem and self-compassion may be important psychological factors associated with women's awareness of domestic violence.ObjectiveThis study examines the relationship between domestic violence awareness, self-compassion, and self-esteem in adult women.MethodsDesigned as a descriptive and correlational study, it includes 2021 women meeting the criteria. The data for the study were collected using the Demographic Information Form, the Domestic Violence Awareness Scale (DVAS), the Self-Compassion Scale (SCS), and the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (RSES). Statistical tests included the Mann-Whitney U test for pairwise comparisons, the Kruskal-Wallis test for between-group comparisons, and Spearman rank correlation analysis for inter-scale relationships. Univariate and multivariate linear regression models were used to investigate the effects of independent variables on dependent scales.ResultsIn this study mean total scores were 19.77 ± 5.12 (RSES), 35.61 ± 7.03 (SCS), and 51.79 ± 8.41 (DVAS). Spearman correlation analysis revealed a significant positive correlation between the SCS and the DVAS, whereas the RSES showed significant negative correlations with both the DVAS and the SCS. In linear regression models, higher self-esteem emerged as the primary independent predictor of domestic violence awareness, while self-compassion played a secondary role once self-esteem was accounted for.ConclusionsThe findings indicate that higher self-esteem and self-compassion are significantly associated with greater domestic violence awareness among women. These psychological resources should be incorporated into educational and counseling interventions to strengthen women's awareness, empowerment, and well-being in personal and productive spheres of life.

papers.title: Expedited partner therapy uptake and STI clearance among cisgender women in a prospective study in Kenya.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: We examined factors associated with expedited partner therapy (EPT) uptake and clearance of Chlamydia trachomatis (CT) and/or Neisseria gonorrhoeae (NG) among women taking HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) in Kenya. METHODS: We conducted a nested analysis of cisgender women enrolled in the dPEP Kenya Study (N=449) who tested positive for CT and/or NG during quarterly testing over one year. Following each positive test, participants received treatment, were offered optional EPT, and returned for a test of cure 2-4 weeks later. Baseline characteristics were compared between participants with and without EPT uptake using chi-square tests. Generalized estimating equation models assessed visit-level correlates of EPT uptake and test-of-cure outcomes while accounting for repeated infections over time. RESULTS: Among 140 participants with CT or NG infection at 209 study visits, 75% (n=105) accepted EPT at least once. Women who accepted EPT were more likely to have an independent income (61.9% p=0.018) and report recent transactional sex (54.3%, p=0.032). At the visit level, having a primary sex partner was positively associated with EPT uptake (OR=2.17, 95% CI=1.01-4.65, p=0.047). Intimate partner violence was associated with lower EPT uptake in multivariable analysis (OR=0.23, 95% CI=0.06-0.95, p=0.042). EPT uptake was not significantly associated with a negative test-of-cure result (OR=2.42, 95% CI=0.89-6.56, p=0.082). CONCLUSIONS: EPT uptake was high among women taking PrEP in Kenya. While partner and relationship factors influenced uptake, EPT was not significantly associated with STI clearance at test of cure.

papers.title: Child abuse and mental health outcomes in Canada: A population-based study with a focus on sex at birth and sexual identity: Violence faite aux enfants et résultats en matière de santé mentale au Canada : étude fondée sur la population axée sur le sexe à la naissance et l'identité sexuelle.
papers.journal: Canadian journal of psychiatry. Revue canadienne de psychiatrie
papers.abstract: BackgroundContemporary nationally representative Canadian statistics on child abuse and mental health outcomes with a focus on sex at birth and sexual identity are essential in determining approaches to prevention and the need for services. The objectives of the current study were to examine the relationship between experiences of abuse during childhood (physical, sexual, exposure to intimate partner violence, and any) and past-year mental health conditions (depression, generalized anxiety disorder, bipolar disorder, social phobia, and suicidal ideation) among adult Canadians, and whether these relationships are moderated by sex at birth and sexual identity.MethodsData were obtained from the cross-sectional 2022 Statistics Canada Mental Health and Access to Care Survey (2022; n = 9,409; 18+ years).FindingsAny child abuse history and each individual child abuse type were associated with an increased likelihood of all poor mental health indicators in the sample after adjusting for sociodemographic covariates (Adjusted Odds Ratio ranging from 1.66 to 4.67). Generally, an increasing dose-response trend was noted for increasing counts of child abuse types (multitype abuse) experienced and increased odds of poor mental health indicators. Sex at birth and sexual identity moderated models for both child abuse and depression and child abuse and social phobia, with stronger associations for females compared to males and for some sexual identities other than heterosexual.InterpretationThe current study provides updated nationally representative data on child abuse history and mental health indicators among adults in Canada. The development and evaluation of child abuse prevention strategies must remain a priority in reducing violence against children and mental health problems among Canadians. Sex at birth and sexual identity differences highlight the need for policies and practices to address the unique needs of women and individuals identifying as lesbia

papers.title: Does the quality of the relationship to parents and peers predict mental health service use during adolescence? A prospective community study.
papers.abstract: Adolescents frequently seek emotional support from parents and peers when experiencing psychological distress. The quality of these relationships may therefore influence their help-seeking behavior and access to professional care, but it is yet unknown whether the quality of the relationship to parents and peers prospectively predict adolescent mental health service use. Guided by the Behavioral Model of Health Service Use, the present study examined whether perceived relationship quality-specifically closeness and conflict with mother, father, and best friend-prospectively predicted use of specialty mental health services. Data were drawn from a Norwegian birth cohort assessed from ages 12 to 18 across four waves (n = 822), using clinical interviews and questionnaires. Results from an autoregressive cross-lagged panel model including a propensity score of potential confounders (prior service use, gender, parental occupation, cohabitation status, parental depression and anxiety, perceived need for help, symptoms of adolescents' emotional problems and disruptive behaviors, impairment, and stressful life events) showed that higher conflict with father predicted lower subsequent service use across age. Other relationship factors (i.e., closeness with father, as well as closeness and conflict with mother and best friend) were unrelated to service use. These findings suggest that father-adolescent conflict may be associated with lower use of specialty mental health services among adolescents and warrant further investigation of the role of fathers in adolescents' help-seeking.
